comparison: Both address the TCGO transgenic characterization (C34, C35). OpenEval finds the characterization sufficient and notes the authors appropriately acknowledge limitations. Peer reviewers find it insufficient, requesting more information about whether the mosaic pattern is stochastic or biologically meaningful.

Both address the regional mapping data (C4, C38-C44, C54, C64). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this data is well-supported and comprehensive. Both note the reproducibility across animals and annotators strengthens the findings.

Both address M1-to-BPN connectivity and corollary discharge claims (C6, C47-C52, C84). OpenEval finds the anatomical evidence strong and the inference reasonable. Peer reviewers find the evidence insufficient as presented, requesting more detail, reproducibility data, and quantitation of colocalization.

Both address the core convergence finding (C3, C36, C37, C53). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly state the data 'unambiguously demonstrate that granule cells are multimodal' and that 'main conclusions are strongly supported.' Peer R1 also includes C55 and C63 which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Both address Slc17a7 transgenic characterization (C25, C26). OpenEval finds the genetic strategy well-validated against database information. Peer reviewers find insufficient data regarding specificity and efficacy of recombination, requesting more description of the transgenic animals.

Both address ECN-BPN proximity and co-termination (C29, C30). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these anatomical observations are supported by the imaging data in Figure 1D. Peer R8 also includes C27, C28 which OpenEval addresses in R1.

Both address major interpretive conclusions and Marr-Albus theory (C5, C94). OpenEval finds these well-supported by the convergence and mapping data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the data 'unambiguously demonstrate that granule cells are multimodal, supporting the predictions of the Marr-Albus theory.' Peer R3 also includes C57, C58 which OpenEval addresses in R15.

Both address computational mechanisms and internal models (C83, C85, C86). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C85-C86 are explicitly speculative but plausible. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, finding the discussion of internal models and automatic coordinate conversion 'not particularly persuasive' and challenging the proposed learning mechanisms. Peer R7 also includes C70-C72, C88-C89 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both address multimodality and computational analogies (C71, C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C72's machine learning analogy is speculative without experimental support. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, finding the computational implications not persuasive.

Both address functional role speculation for cerebellar regions (C88, C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but untested hypotheses. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, challenging the functional implications of the anatomical findings.

OpenEval evaluates prior work and methodological critiques (C17-C19, C59-C62) as SUPPORTED, finding the characterization of prior literature accurate and the critique well-justified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims about unlabeled inputs (C67, C68) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caution and honest acknowledgment of limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates hierarchical processing speculation (C93) as UNCERTAIN, noting it lacks direct experimental evidence despite anatomical observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background knowledge claims (C1-C2, C8-C11, C20-C21, C23-C24, C31-C32, C45, C69, C73-C80, C87, C91) as SUPPORTED, noting these are appropriately cited established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical context and comparative evidence (C12-C16, C22, C57-C58, C65-C66, C70, C7) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and accurate interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C57-C58 and C70 appear in peer R3 and R7 respectively with different claim groupings.
OpenEval evaluates methodological inference about visualization capability (C33) as SUPPORTED, validated by successful execution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates summary statements of major findings (C56, C92, C96) as SUPPORTED. C56 overlaps with peer R2 which supports the regional mapping, but no direct peer evaluation of these specific summary claims found.
OpenEval evaluates future research recommendation (C95) as SUPPORTED, noting it follows logically from findings and incomplete labeling. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
